project.purpose: Own one bounded Agent Run's durable cognition, provider/tool interaction, action admission, effect binding, recovery, and completion proposal without owning caller Task meaning or Runtime physical truth.

nodes.label: RunContract
nodes.responsibility: Bind one exact Harness Run contract, provider/tool affordances, budgets, and caller context.
acceptance: A run is independently identifiable and bounded.

nodes.label: ContextProjection
nodes.responsibility: Compile current model cognition from durable working set, current ingress, and attempt context rather than replaying complete history.
acceptance: Context can be rebuilt from bounded owned sources.

nodes.label: ActionAdmission
nodes.responsibility: Turn model/tool proposals into exact admitted actions without treating intent as authority.
acceptance: Unadmitted proposals cannot become tool effects.

nodes.label: EffectBinding
nodes.responsibility: Bind admitted tool intents to physical evidence while preserving ambiguous-effect semantics.
acceptance: Lost response does not cause blind duplicate effect.

nodes.label: HarnessProviderSPI
nodes.responsibility: Expose a prepared-attempt executor seam so alternate mature harness engines can be integrated without moving Task/Runtime authority.
acceptance: A second harness implementation can run behind the same caller-facing contract.

slices.objective: Prove a Harness Provider SPI with one alternate executor adapter while preserving Run/Task/Runtime authority boundaries.
acceptance: Native/current harness and one alternate adapter satisfy the same prepared-run contract without schema changes in caller Task or Runtime.
slices.nextAction: Inventory current provider seams and implement the smallest adapter proof rather than a new harness.

gaps: A general alternate-harness adapter has not yet been accepted by evidence in this plan.

review.notes: Initial project-native LEGO planning projection. It does not replace owner-native architecture or evidence.

sharedCatalog.note: Optional shared coordinates only; project-native semantics remain authoritative.
